QuestionStmt.S: The statements $p$, $q$ and $r$ have truth values True, False and False respectively. The truth values of the logical statement $[ \sim (p \land \sim q) \lor (q \lor \sim r) ]$ and its dual are, respectively

Solution.S:
Step 1: Given $p = T$, $q = F$, $r = F$.

Step 2: Evaluate the given statement: $\sim (p \land \sim q) \lor (q \lor \sim r)$.

$\sim q = T$, so $p \land \sim q = T \land T = T$. Hence $\sim (p \land \sim q) = F$.

$\sim r = T$, so $q \lor \sim r = F \lor T = T$.

Thus the whole statement = $F \lor T = T$.

Step 3: Find the dual of the statement.

The statement is $\sim (p \land \sim q) \lor (q \lor \sim r)$.

Dual: replace $\lor$ with $\land$ and $\land$ with $\lor$.

First term: $\sim (p \land \sim q)$ becomes $\sim (p \lor \sim q)$.

Second term: $q \lor \sim r$ becomes $q \land \sim r$.

The whole expression becomes $\sim (p \lor \sim q) \land (q \land \sim r)$.

Evaluate: $p \lor \sim q = T \lor T = T$, so $\sim (p \lor \sim q) = F$.

$q \land \sim r = F \land T = F$.

Thus dual = $F \land F = F$.

Therefore, the truth values are True for the original and False for its dual.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\text{True, False}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
